semantic_review.what_changed: The core value accompanying an `incomplete` work result changes from `indeterminate` to `falsified` (on the predicate 'a candidate is available'); the successor forbids reading it as `indeterminate`. Other variants, totality and exclusivity conserved.
semantic_review.counterexample: A Worker's bounded execution ends before any candidate exists, with no prohibition or refusal. Predecessor: the work result `incomplete` carries `indeterminate`, and a declared conjunction consuming it stays `indeterminate` (an open residual). Successor: the same stop carries `falsified` with the stop basis as counterexample; the conjunction over 'a candidate is available' is falsified and the result may never be read as `indeterminate`.
semantic_review.smallest_repair: Record a replacement relation for `incomplete`'s core value (`indeterminate` -> `falsified` on 'a candidate is available') instead of `conserved`, or restore the predecessor pairing.
semantic_review.executive_note: The change the reader found, incomplete's core value indeterminate -> falsified on 'a candidate is available', is the clause the frontier split to the child row #work-result-disjointness-and-incomplete-pairing, a proposed replacement under question Q1; the parent row is 'conserved, save the two clauses split to the child row below'. The batch packet did not show the child row. No further change; the reader's verdict stands on the parent as read.
